q: What does a Belgian importer's CBAM authority mean for an Indian supplier?
title: Belgian importers: CBAM authority
short: Belgian importers above 50 tonnes a year need authorised CBAM declarant status. Belgium handles CBAM at federal level, through the Climate Change Service of the Federal Public Service for Health, Food Chain Safety and Environment. Its guidance comes in Dutch, French and English, and your buyer will still need your installation data.
audience: Indian exporters of steel, aluminium, cement and fertiliser selling to buyers in Belgium, and the buyers' purchasing teams

ul: One federal authority covers the whole country, not the regions.
It publishes CBAM pages in Dutch, French and English, so a Belgian buyer may send requests in any of the three.
Hydrogen imports have no 50 tonne exemption, which matters for importers around Antwerp.

sections.h: What your buyer will ask you for
ul: The installation that made the goods and the calendar year of production.
Specific embedded emissions per tonne, with a verification report from an EU-accredited verifier if actual data is used.
The data for the free allocation adjustment and, where one applies, the carbon price paid in India.

sections.h: If you cannot send verified data
p: Your buyer can still declare using the Commission's default values, which carry a mark-up and usually cost more. A Belgian buyer facing that bill will push for your actual figures or compare you with suppliers who have them.

senseible: Senseible keeps supplier invoices and the emissions data that comes with them in one dated, fingerprinted record per shipment, and its CBAM cost calculator estimates certificate cost from 2026 to 2034. Senseible does not verify emissions, register declarants or file CBAM declarations.
